Photos.Caption: Weber bottom 'P' vents - best control of temperature for smokes

Results.ReviewText:
This is my third 22" weber in 40 years.  My favorite feature of this grill is the air slots in the bottom.. Same wiper assembly but the air slots look like a "P" shape - which allows much more control for low temperature cooks like smoking ribs, pork shoulders and beef brisket SLOWLY.  Love it!  

My only gripe is that the ash basket changed from a left to right release, to a "squeeze-of-the-handle" to release straight down.  Good idea, but the strength required to squeeze the handle far enough for the release of the basket is not reasonable.  

One design suggestion: instead of putting the thermometer opposite of top vent, put it closer to the top vent.  This allows temperature to be taken over the meat where the top vent will be to draw smoke over the meat - opposite the fire.  As it, there is no good way to position the top vent over the meat without the thermometer right over the fire opposite the meat.  As is, the thermometer is no good for judging inside temperature for smokes because it reads too high right over the coals.

Great quality and still the best for grilling AND smoking all-in-one!
Results.Title: My Third Weber

Results.ReviewText: Love my new weber grill.  Would have given it a 5 star rating with one exception. Results.Title: Great grill except the grate.

Results.ReviewText: This grill may be new but I have owned Weber kettle grills for over 25 years.  They are by far one of the best grills ever.  I can cook everything from hotdogs to turkeys in this grill and they come out absolutely delicious.  I have never been a fan of gas grilling because I can never get that flavor that I and everyone I have grilled for loves.  Grilling is an art and this grill helps me make masterpieces.  Thanks Weber for making a fantastic product.
Results.Title: My all time favorite grill

ClientResponses.Response:
We appreciate your feedback. We are so sorry to hear about your experience. We are here to help. 

It’s completely normal for smoke to come out from between the lid and bowl on a new kettle, and it won’t negatively affect your ability to grill or smoke great food.

The lid and bowls on a brand new kettle often do not form a perfect seal.

Over time, the lid and bowl will form a natural seal of carbon that builds up by using the grill.

However, there may always be a little bit of movement between the lid and bowl, and smoke will occasionally escape, depending on what you're grilling.

Also, on models that come with a lid thermometer, it isn’t unheard of for some smoke to escape from around the thermometer. Reinstalling the thermometer and thermometer bezel to get a better seal might help, but over time the carbon will build up and create a natural seal which will minimize the amount of escaping smoke.

It is hard to say how long it will take for the seal to build up, because it depends on how often you grill as well as what you grill, but it will build up eventually, and in the meantime there is nothing to worry about. 

Our Care team will be reaching out to follow up. Please look for an outreach email from us soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText:
I'm 67 years old and have never grilled anything besides hot dogs and hamburgers on a variety of big box store grills. Grilling was just a necessary chore so we could eat. Then my wife got me this gem.  
All of a sudden I WANT to grill. I've made several steaks (for the first time in my life) that came out perfect. She also got me Weber's Greatest Hits and Weber's Smoke cookbooks and frankly, I had no idea I could actually cook. I use the Weber chimney to get the coals started, and once I drop them the vents do a great job controlling the temperature. Keeping it clean is simple too, especially getting rid of the ashes.  
Whether you're a novice or a veteran griller, I guarantee you will be happy with this grill.

Results.ReviewText:
It cooks perfectly fine, but the build quality of this grill is abysmally low. In only a summer of ownership, I had the main drag handle fail on one side due to a poor weld. I contacted their support team about this and then a game was played where the support member I was speaking to tried to deny my warranty because the handle broke when I was moving it. I had to defend myself in an email and argue this was a manufacturing defect and after that I was given a replacement bowl.

The piece that failed was the spot weld where the main handle connects to the bowl. The paint flaked from normal cooking heat cycles and exposed the small spot weld to rust apart. 

I also discovered during the replacement of my bowl (my wife built this for me originally) the top bowl handle does not bolt and nut together, causing looseness that can't be repaired. It's a 1/4-20 thread with a stamped piece of metal meant to act like a nut pushed down into the threads. 1/4-20 nuts are so cheap it's ridiculous.

Overall my experience with this grill was great until I had a problem, now when I think of Weber I think of an American grill company that sold out and cheapened their product.
Results.Title: Good for cooking, but plagued by poor quality.

14401001.Name: 22” Original Kettle® Premium Charcoal Grill
14401001.Description: Some things never go out of style—like the smoky flavor of charcoal, the sizzle of a summer cookout, and the iconic silhouette of the 22" Original Kettle® Premium Charcoal Grill. This grill features a built-in lid thermometer to monitor the temperature inside the grill, and a hinged, plated-steel cooking grate flips up on either side allowing you to easily add more fuel while cooking. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retains heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs. Because some grills don’t just cook food, they make memories.· Porcelain-enameled finish is scratch and rust-resistant· Room to cook for 6-8 people· Hinged, plated-steel cooking grate· Lid thermometer makes it easy to see grill temperature· Adjustable lid and bowl dampers let you control temperature· Lid hook to hang lid on bowl while cooking· 2 tool hooks included on bowl handle· One-Touch™ cleaning system sweeps ash into enclosed catcher· Easy to move on two durable, all-weather wheels· Heat-resistant lid and bowl handles· Bottom, wire storage shelf· Durable fuel grate· 3 aluminum legs are rust-resistant· 10-year limited warranty
